headline: EU regulatory briefing: CSRD assurance, ESPR passports, and CBAM rules
summary: This week's key updates include a Commission consultation on CSRD limited assurance standards and technical specifications for the ESPR Digital Product Passport registry. Rules were also finalized for deducting third-country carbon costs under CBAM, alongside an official corrigendum to the EU Machinery Regulation.

items.title: Commission consults on CSRD limited assurance standards
items.what: The European Commission launched a consultation on limited assurance standards for reporting under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive.
items.meaning: Directly impacts your FY2027 CSRD reporting by setting expectations for external auditor verification of sustainability disclosures.
items.action: Review the consultation details with internal audit and sustainability teams to prepare verification workflows.

sources.title: EU CSRD: Commission consults on limited assurance standards, Julia Voskoboinikova

items.title: Technical resources published for ESPR Digital Product Passport registry
items.what: The European Commission published six technical resources detailing how businesses will connect to the official Digital Product Passport registry.
items.meaning: Relevant for preparing your tool and battery platform data architecture to comply with upcoming ESPR and battery passport mandates.
items.action: Share technical resources with IT and supply chain teams to plan data integration with Chinese suppliers.

sources.title: EU Publishes Digital Product Passport Registry Documentation
Commission publishes six technical resources for companies connecting to the digital product passport registry

items.title: EU adopts rules for third-country carbon price deductions under CBAM
items.what: The European Commission adopted rules for deducting carbon prices paid outside the EU, with reports indicating recognition of China's carbon market.
items.meaning: While finished tools are currently outside CBAM scope, proposed downstream extensions to steel and aluminium products could impact imports from China.
items.action: Monitor proposed CBAM downstream product extensions and review supplier carbon data in China.

items.title: Official corrigendum published for EU Machinery Regulation
items.what: An official corrigendum to EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 was published in the Official Journal of the EU.
items.meaning: As the brand manufacturer under EU law, text corrections may affect technical files and compliance readiness ahead of 2027.
items.action: Review corrected text against ongoing Machinery Regulation compliance preparations for January 2027.
